note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in ID.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Oregon Trail–Bear Lake Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 89 from Bear Lake near Fish Haven north to Montpelier, US 30 through Soda Springs, Old US 30 via Bancroft and Lava Hot Springs to McCammon

facts.fact: Begins at Bear Lake on US 89 near Fish Haven, runs north through Montpelier onto US 30, through Soda Springs, then Old US 30 through Bancroft to Lava Hot Springs and McCammon; 92.8 miles.
The Bank of Montpelier is described as the last standing bank robbed by Butch Cassidy and his gang.
Soda Springs has what the page calls the world's only captive geyser; the National Oregon/California Trail Center is on the route.

byways.review: Catalog line is 111 mapped miles against 92.8 listed by Visit Idaho; check the line does not run past McCammon or include extra spurs.

byways.name: Sacajawea Historic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 33 from I-15 exit 143 west to Idaho 28, then Idaho 28 northwest 120 miles to Salmon

facts.fact: Begins at I-15 exit 143, follows Idaho 33 about 12 miles to Idaho 28, then Idaho 28 northwest 120 miles to Salmon; 135 miles.
Runs parallel to the Continental Divide through the Lemhi River Valley.

Stops include the Charcoal Kilns Interpretive Site near Leadore and the Sacajawea Interpretive, Cultural & Educational Center in Salmon, which tells Sacajawea's story and her impact on the Corps of Discovery.

byways.name: White Pine Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 3 from I-90 south through St. Maries to Idaho 6, then Idaho 6 to US 95 at Potlatch

facts.fact: Runs from the junction of I-90 and Idaho 3 south on Idaho 3 to Idaho 6, then southwest to US 95 at Potlatch; about 80 miles.
Passes marshland spotted with lakes fed by the lower Coeur d'Alene River before crossing the St. Maries and St. Joe rivers.
Sites include the 19th-century Cataldo Mission at Old Mission State Park, and Potlatch, once home to the world's largest white pine mill.

byways.name: St. Joe River Scenic Byway
byways.where: Forest Highway 50 east from St. Maries along the St. Joe River 75 miles, then 14 miles north to the Montana line on Road 218

facts.fact: Follows Forest Highway 50 east from St. Maries along the St. Joe River for 75 miles, then 14 miles north to the Idaho-Montana border; 87.3 miles.
Bald eagles and osprey nest in the cottonwoods along the river and fish its waters.
Stops include Marble Creek Historical Park and the Historic Avery Ranger Station.

byways.name: Ponderosa Pine Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 21 from Boise northeast through Idaho City and Lowman to Idaho 75 at Stanley

facts.fact: Follows Idaho 21 from Boise through historic Idaho City and Lowman to the junction with Idaho 75 at Stanley; 131 miles.
Follows a portion of the South Fork of the Payette River.
Avalanche conditions exist in the Banner Summit area and road closures may occur; Boise Basin Museum covers Idaho City's gold rush.

byways.name: Wildlife Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.where: Banks-Lowman Road between Idaho 55 at Banks and Idaho 21 at Lowman, via Garden Valley and Crouch

facts.fact: Follows the South Fork of the Payette River along Banks-Lowman Road between Banks (Idaho 55) and Lowman (Idaho 21); 35.8 miles.
Services in Garden Valley, Lowman and Crouch; activities include whitewater rafting, wildlife viewing and fishing.
Joins both the Ponderosa Pine and Payette River scenic byways.

byways.name: Elk River Backcountry Byway
byways.where: From Idaho 7 and Wells Bench Road at Orofino over the Dent Bridge to Elk River and Idaho 8

facts.fact: Begins in Orofino at Idaho 7 and Wells Bench Road, crosses the North Fork of the Clearwater on the Dent Bridge, and ends in Elk River at Idaho 8; 54 miles.
The Dent Bridge over Dworshak Reservoir is described as the state's tallest bridge.
Runs through evergreen forests of the Clearwater Mountains; Elk Creek Falls is nearby.

byways.name: Lake Coeur d'Alene Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 97 from I-90 at Wolf Lodge Bay south along the east shore to Idaho 3 near Harrison

facts.fact: Follows Idaho 97 from I-90 to Idaho 3; a two-lane, paved winding road with few passing lanes.
Peak eagle watching is in December and January.
Idaho 97 runs along the east shore of Lake Coeur d'Alene through Harrison and meets I-90 at Wolf Lodge Bay; the whole highway is the byway.

byways.review: Visit Idaho gives 25.2 miles; Wikipedia gives 35.7 miles for the whole of Idaho 97. Catalog maps 36.

byways.name: Peaks to Craters Scenic Byway
byways.where: From Idaho 75 and US 20 near Carey through Arco, then US 93 through Mackay to Idaho 75 near Challis

facts.fact: Runs from the Idaho 75/US 20 junction near Carey through Arco to the US 93/Idaho 75 junction; 143 miles. Services in Carey, Arco, Mackay and Challis.
Passes Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve near Arco, and Arco is called the first city lit by atomic energy.
Mount Borah in the Lost River Mountains is Idaho's tallest peak at 12,662 feet.

byways.review: Catalog tags this 'Idaho State Scenic Backway'; Visit Idaho and ITD GIS list it as a state scenic byway.

byways.name: Lewis and Clark Backcountry Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Backcountry Byway; BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: Loop east of Idaho 28 at Tendoy, about 20 miles southeast of Salmon, to Lemhi Pass

facts.fact: A single-lane gravel road with pullouts, entered by turning east from Idaho 28 at the Tendoy store; buses, RVs and trailers are not recommended on some sections; 35.9 miles.
A 36-mile loop on the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail and the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail.
The landscape looks much the same as when the Lewis and Clark Expedition passed through in 1805.
Nearby: Lemhi Pass, the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail and Sharkey Hot Springs near Tendoy.

byways.review: Lemhi Pass is named as an attraction on the Visit Idaho page; the BLM page links a 2016 guide PDF with segment detail. Visit Idaho page used as a second source.

byways.name: Thousand Springs Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 30 from near Bliss southeast through Hagerman, Buhl and Twin Falls to Idaho 50, then north to I-84; alternate via US 93

facts.fact: Starts near Bliss and follows US 30 southeast through Twin Falls to Idaho 50, then north to I-84; 65.4 miles. Services in Bliss, Hagerman, Buhl, Kimberly and Twin Falls.
Thousand Springs State Park is made up of six park units with waterfalls and trails.
Nearby sites include Malad Gorge, Shoshone Falls, the Perrine Bridge and Hagerman Fossil Beds National Monument.

byways.name: Teton Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 31 from Swan Valley to Victor, Idaho 33 north through Driggs and Tetonia, Idaho 32 to Ashton

facts.fact: Begins on Idaho 31 at Swan Valley, goes to Idaho 33 at Victor, north on Idaho 33 to Idaho 32, and ends at Idaho 47 at Ashton; 67.6 miles.
Described as 'the quiet side of the Grand Teton Mountains', with views that turn into far-reaching fields.
Stops include Fall Creek Falls in Swan Valley, the Teton Geo Center in Driggs, and the Ashton-Tetonia Trail on a former Union Pacific rail spur.

byways.name: Owyhee Uplands Backcountry Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Backcountry Byway; BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: Gravel route from Idaho 78 near Grand View west to Jordan Valley, Oregon

facts.fact: Reached from Idaho 78 near Grand View or from Jordan Valley, Oregon; about 101 miles of mostly one to one-and-a-half lane gravel road.
Crosses desert landscapes and juniper woodlands with views of the Owyhee Mountains; only partial services in Grand View and Jordan Valley.
BLM gives 92 miles in Idaho plus 12 in Oregon across the Owyhee Plateau, with habitat for over 180 species of birds and mammals.

byways.review: Last 12 miles are in Oregon; catalog lists it as ID only.

byways.name: Fort Henry Historic Byway
byways.where: From US 20 at north Rexburg via Salem Highway to the St. Anthony Sand Dunes, north to Island Park, back via US 20 Business to St. Anthony, old US 191 through Chester to Ashton

facts.fact: Begins at the North Rexburg US 20 exit, goes by Salem Highway to the St. Anthony Sand Dunes, north and east to Island Park, then St. Anthony on US 20 Business and old US 191 past Chester to Ashton; 90.4 miles.
The St. Anthony Sand Dunes cover 10,600 acres of white quartz sand up to 400 feet high.
Henry's Fork of the Snake River is known for fly fishing; the A-2 road is unplowed in winter and becomes a snowmobile trail.

byways.name: Main Oregon Trail Backcountry Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Backcountry Byway; BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: From Glenns Ferry (I-84 exit 121) northwest to Bonneville Point southeast of Boise

facts.fact: Starts at Glenns Ferry; 102 miles, one-third paved and two-thirds gravel, about 6 hours.
Three Island Crossing State Park in Glenns Ferry marks one of the most arduous river crossings for pioneers.
BLM describes the route from Glenns Ferry to Bonneville Point southeast of Boise, where visitors can see Oregon Trail ruts.

byways.review: ITD GIS names this 'Oregon Trail Back Country Byway'. Catalog maps 88 miles against 102 listed.

byways.name: Wild Horse Trail Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 95 from downtown Sandpoint north through Bonners Ferry, then Idaho 1 to the Canadian border at Porthill

facts.fact: Begins in downtown Sandpoint on Lake Pend Oreille, follows US 95 north through Bonners Ferry and Idaho 1 to the border at Porthill; 35.9 miles.
Follows the 'Wild Horse Trail', important to the Kootenai Tribe and to settlers as the area grew through the gold rush era.
Passes the McArthur Lake Wildlife Corridor; the Kootenai National Wildlife Refuge is nearby. Part of the International Selkirk Loop.

byways.review: Visit Idaho gives 35.9 miles, which looks short for Sandpoint to Porthill; check against catalog (48 mapped).

byways.name: Northwest Passage Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 12 from Lewiston to the Montana line, plus Idaho 13 from Kooskia to Grangeville and US 95

facts.fact: Begins in Lewiston and follows US 12 northeast to the Idaho-Montana border for 175 miles, and Idaho 13 from Kooskia to Grangeville; 202 miles, Idaho's longest byway.
Follows the path of Lewis and Clark through north central Idaho, up the Clearwater River canyon, with numerous Nez Perce historical sites and the Camas Prairie.
Named an All-American Road.

byways.review: Visit Idaho text dates the Lewis and Clark passage to 1803 (it was 1805); not used.

byways.name: Lower Payette River Heritage Byway
byways.where: Idaho 52 from the Snake River at Payette east through Emmett to Horseshoe Bend

facts.fact: Begins on the banks of the Snake River and goes east on Highway 52 along the Payette River through Payette, Emmett and Horseshoe Bend; 56.8 miles.
Sites include the Montour Wildlife Management Area and Black Canyon Reservoir and Dam.
Seasonal fruit picking at orchards along the route.

byways.review: Not in catalog. ITD GIS value is 'Lower Payette River Heritage Scenic Byway' (one record, Type Primary, Designation State).

byways.name: Mesa Falls Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 47 from Ashton northeast to the old Bear Gulch ski area, then Forest Route 294 to US 20

facts.fact: Starts in Ashton on Idaho 47, runs 12.4 miles to the old Bear Gulch Ski Area site, then Forest Service Route 294 to US 20; 28.2 miles. FS 294 is closed to cars in winter and becomes a snowmobile route.
Upper and Lower Mesa Falls are each as tall as a 10-story building; there is a historic Mesa Falls Visitor Center.
The upper falls pour over remnants of an ancient volcanic super-eruption, in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest.

byways.name: Western Heritage Historic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 69 from I-84 exit 44 at Meridian south through Kuna, Swan Falls Road to Swan Falls Dam, then west toward Celebration Park

facts.fact: Begins at exit 44 in Meridian, follows Idaho 69 south through Kuna, then Swan Falls Road through the Morley Nelson conservation area to Swan Falls Dam and west toward Celebration Park; 38.8 miles.
Once a route for miners and homesteaders.
Celebration Park is Idaho's only archaeological park; the Birds of Prey NCA has the greatest concentration of nesting raptors in North America.

byways.review: Catalog maps 28 miles against 38.8 listed; the Celebration Park leg may be missing.

byways.name: Payette River Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 55 from Eagle north through Horseshoe Bend, Banks, Cascade and McCall to US 95 at New Meadows

facts.fact: Follows Idaho 55 from Eagle to US 95 at New Meadows along the Payette River through the Boise and Payette national forests; 114 miles.
North of Banks the highway crosses the river on the Rainbow Bridge, built in 1933, then follows the North Fork.
The road follows the east shore of Cascade Reservoir and reaches McCall at the south shore of Payette Lake.

byways.name: Hells Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 71 west from Cambridge to Oxbow Bridge, then north on the Idaho side of the Snake to Hells Canyon Dam; also Brownlee Dam to Oxbow

facts.fact: Runs west from Cambridge on Idaho 71 to the Oxbow Bridge near Copperfield, Oregon, then north along Idaho's side of the Snake River to Hells Canyon Dam; 62.4 miles.
Follows the east side of Hells Canyon, called North America's deepest river gorge.
Wildlife includes bears, bald eagles and bighorn sheep; sturgeon fishing and jet boat tours.

byways.review: Catalog maps only 22 miles against 62.4 listed; probably only Idaho 71 is drawn. ITD GIS has one 'Hells Canyon Scenic Byway' record.

byways.name: Snake River Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.where: Back roads from Walters Ferry on Idaho 45 north through Marsing, Homedale and Parma to Centennial Park on the Snake River

facts.fact: Begins at Walters Ferry on State Highway 45 and runs north on roads including Map Rock Road and Chicken Dinner Road; about 70 miles.
Passes orchards and vineyards of the Sunnyslope Wine Trail.
Attractions include Map Rock, Old Fort Boise Park in Parma and Deer Flat National Wildlife Refuge.

byways.review: ITD GIS also carries 11 'Proposed Snake River Canyon Scenic Byway' segments beside the designated ones; catalog maps 52 miles against about 70 listed.

byways.name: Lost Gold Trails Loop
byways.where: From the A-2/Red Road junction east of Dubois north on Old Highway 91 to Spencer, east on Spencer-Idmon Road to the Fort Henry byway

facts.fact: Begins at the A-2/Red Road junction east of Dubois, goes north on Old Highway 91 to Spencer, then east on Spencer/Idmon Road to the Fort Henry Historic Byway; 52 miles.
Follows an early gold rush route; the area moved from gold to opal mining and visitors can still dig for opals.
Passes Beaver Canyon and the Heritage Hall Museum; two roads close in winter.

byways.name: Pioneer Historic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 91 from the Utah line, Idaho 34 north through Preston and Grace to US 30, east to Soda Springs, then Idaho 34 to Wyoming

facts.fact: Begins at the Utah state line, follows US 91 then Idaho 34 north to US 30 and Soda Springs, then Idaho 34 toward Wyoming; 114 miles.
Idaho 34 between Soda Springs and the Wyoming border may close in winter from heavy snow.
Attractions include the Soda Springs captive geyser, Red Rock Pass and Chesterfield, with 27 original 1880s structures on the National Register.

byways.review: Visit Idaho lists Red Rock Pass as an attraction; it is on US 91 north of the Idaho 34 turn, so it is left out of the blurb.

byways.name: Salmon River Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 93 from the Montana line south through North Fork, Salmon and Challis, then Idaho 75 west to Stanley

facts.fact: Runs from the Montana state line south on US 93 to Challis, then west to Stanley on Idaho 75; 163 miles.
Follows the Salmon River, with rafting on the main Salmon and the Middle Fork.
Land of the Yankee Fork State Park includes the ghost towns of Bayhorse, Bonanza and Custer.

byways.name: Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 200 from US 95 north of Sandpoint through Hope and Clark Fork to the Montana line

facts.fact: Follows Idaho 200 along the rocky northern shore of Lake Pend Oreille from US 95 north of Sandpoint to the Montana line; 34.5 miles, two-lane with scenic turnouts.
Lake Pend Oreille is Idaho's largest and deepest lake.
Services in Sandpoint, Ponderay and Clark Fork, partial services in Hope.

byways.name: Panhandle Historic Rivers Passage
byways.where: US 2 from the Washington line at Oldtown through Priest River to Sandpoint

facts.fact: Begins at the Washington state line and follows US 2 to Sandpoint along the north shore of the Pend Oreille River; 29.9 miles. Southern portion of the International Selkirk Loop.
The landscape was shaped by the Ice Age and the Great Missoula Floods.
Albeni Falls Dam Visitor Center and the Pend Oreille Wildlife Management Area are along the way.

byways.review: ITD GIS designation field reads 'All American' because it is part of the International Selkirk Loop.

byways.name: City of Rocks Backcountry Byway
byways.where: Idaho 77 from Albion south through Elba and Almo to City of Rocks, then gravel north along Birch Creek to Oakley and Idaho 27

facts.fact: Begins in Albion on Idaho 77, goes south through Elba and Almo to City of Rocks National Reserve, then north along Birch Creek to Oakley and Idaho 27; 49.4 miles, with gravel between Almo and Oakley.
Runs through the Albion Mountains among towering granite spires; Elephant Rock is a named formation.
Nearby: Castle Rocks State Park, Pomerelle Mountain Resort, Lake Cleveland and the Oakley Historic District.

byways.name: Gold Rush Historic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 11 from US 12 at Greer north through Weippe and Pierce to Headquarters

facts.fact: Begins at the junction of US 12 and Idaho 11 at Greer and runs north to Headquarters; 42.3 miles.
Pierce is where gold was first found in Idaho; the Historic Pierce Chinese Cemetery is on the route.
Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark sites, the Weippe Discovery Center, and views of the Clearwater Valley and grain fields.

byways.name: International Selkirk Loop – Idaho Portion
byways.where: US 2 from Oldtown to Sandpoint, US 95 to Bonners Ferry, Idaho 1 to Porthill; combines the Panhandle Historic Rivers Passage and Wild Horse Trail byways

facts.fact: The loop spans 280 miles across Idaho, Washington and British Columbia; the Idaho section is 89.2 miles from Oldtown via US 2, Sandpoint, US 95 to Bonners Ferry and Idaho 1 to Porthill.
The Idaho portion combines the Wild Horse Trail Scenic Byway and the Panhandle Historic Rivers Passage, and nearly all of it follows rivers and lakeshores.
The International Selkirk Loop is one of 32 All-American Roads.

byways.review: Visit Idaho lists this as a separate entry though it is made of two other state byways in this list; avoid drawing twice. Visit Idaho's own count is 31 byways.

byways.name: Sawtooth Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Idaho Scenic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Idaho 75 from Shoshone north through Hailey, Ketchum and over Galena Summit to Stanley

facts.fact: Runs from Shoshone to Stanley on Idaho 75 through the Boulder Mountains to the Sawtooth Range; 116 miles. Services in Bellevue, Hailey, Ketchum, Sun Valley and Stanley.
Galena Summit, Redfish Lake and the Sawtooth National Recreation Area are along the way; fishing on the Big Wood River.
Noted for stargazing; the Central Idaho Dark Sky Reserve is nearby.

issues: No current ITD web page lists the program; Visit Idaho is the working list (32 entries, but it calls the total 31 because the International Selkirk Loop entry duplicates Panhandle Historic Rivers Passage plus Wild Horse Trail). Visit Idaho returns 403 to curl; read via WebFetch.
Lower Payette River Heritage Byway (Idaho 52) is not in the catalog; draw from ITD GIS BywayName = 'Lower Payette River Heritage Scenic Byway'.

Mileage mismatches catalog vs Visit Idaho: Hells Canyon 22 vs 62.4 (likely only Idaho 71 drawn), Oregon Trail-Bear Lake 111 vs 92.8, Main Oregon Trail 88 vs 102, Western Heritage 28 vs 38.8, Snake River Canyon 52 vs about 70, Wild Horse Trail 48 vs 35.9 (Visit Idaho figure itself looks low).
International Selkirk Loop catalog entry is ID,WA at 151 miles; the full loop is 280 miles including British Columbia. Idaho part overlaps two other members; avoid double drawing.
Catalog labels Peaks to Craters as 'Idaho State Scenic Backway'; Visit Idaho and ITD GIS treat it as a state scenic byway on paved US 93/US 20/US 26.

Visit Idaho's Northwest Passage page dates Lewis and Clark to 1803 (should be 1805); its White Pine page mentions Banner Summit avalanches, which belong to the Ponderosa Pine byway. Both errors avoided in blurbs.
Visit Idaho byway URLs sit under odd activity categories (ziplining, horseback-riding); they work today but may move.

Teton, Mesa Falls and Sawtooth also carry National Forest Scenic Byway status and Lewis and Clark, Owyhee Uplands and Main Oregon Trail are BLM Back Country Byways; all are state members, so no separate program was needed.
